reason: Crossing orbits should bring rocky planetesimals together, starting the growth of a rocky embryo.
expectation: I expect collisions or accumulation to produce a larger rocky body, though some impacts may instead break bodies apart.

alternatives.reason: Breaking the differentiated world could supply useful fragments, but I want to start growing an embryo first.

effect: The impacts produced several growing embryos, so I can now pursue their further growth.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the expected accumulation, with multiple embryos growing at once.
reason: Gravitational focusing should help the embryos gather more material and grow.
expectation: I expect a larger rocky embryo or faster accretion, though the precise result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Adding planetesimals also seems useful, but gravitational focusing may advance embryo growth more directly.

effect: Gravitational focusing produced an embryo that can now attract rocky fragments more effectively.
reaction: The link between increasing mass and faster growth makes sense.
reason: Adding rocky fragments should help the strongly attracting embryo grow.
expectation: I expect a larger rocky body, though I don't know whether it will be the young Earth or another embryo.

alternatives.reason: Adding planetesimals could also grow embryos, but I want to follow the strongly attracting one.

effect: The rocky fragments produced the proto-Earth, but it still needs a source of volatiles.
reaction: It is useful to see which embryo becomes the Earth we follow.
reason: Adding planetesimals to the other embryos should advance the goal of growing another rocky body.
expectation: I expect another larger rocky embryo, though the exact result is uncertain.

reaction: Theia's identification is intriguing, especially with its uncertain properties acknowledged.
reason: This is the only offered combination; breaking the differentiated body may provide material for the proto-Earth.

reaction: The connection to iron meteorites is interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination; adding the core fragments should contribute metal to the growing Earth.

reaction: The qualification about other possible sources makes the outcome more informative.

mostWorthwhile.text: Growing the strongly attracting embryo illustrated how gravitational focusing makes further accretion more effective.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence of adding rocky fragments and then metal felt somewhat linear, especially once only one combination was offered.

surprise.text: The other embryo became Theia; its identification was intriguing, particularly with its uncertain properties acknowledged.

arbitrary.text: Breaking the metal-cored body seemed useful, but its connection to the remaining volatile goal was unclear when it was the only offered combination.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the story handles Theia’s encounter with Earth, especially given the uncertainty it acknowledges.
